prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production-oriented PIXEL ART asset sheet for Goat Out, a top-down 3/4 overhead dungeon action game. The first attached image is the EXISTING GAME SPRITE STYLE: copy its chunky readable pixel clusters and restrained shading, NOT its subjects. Second attached image is game camera context. Match that perspective, front and top visible, orthographic not isometric diamonds. Physical game tile 32 world px, prop grain 1.35 world px per art texel (~24 art pixels per tile); ordinary enemy source ~26px extent shown at 36 world px. This is an enlarged pixel-art sheet: all objects must look like genuinely tiny sprites enlarged by nearest neighbor, large square pixels, few colors, 3 shade steps per material, dark charcoal colored outlines, upper-left light, small hard highlights. Strictly no smooth painting, no tiny decorative detail, no antialiasing, no gradients, no bloom, no photorealism. Muted iron grey, soot brown, tarnished brass/ochre, restrained oxidized teal; small amber/red hazard accents. Shapes and silhouette over texture. All objects fully visible with roomy empty gutters; no labels, no text, no UI, no watermarks. Asset: modular factory walls sheet. 2 rows of exactly 4 separated wall modules. TOP ROW: soot brick wall with riveted iron cap straight 3-tile strip; matching outside corner; matching inside corner; matching doorway frame. BOTTOM ROW: heavier foundry wall with iron lower panels and soot brick upper, straight 3-tile strip; matching outside corner; matching inside corner; matching wide doorway frame. Each 1 tile wall has 24 source texels along it and about 24 texels tall, a top cap and a visible vertical face, same perspective as game screenshot. Sparse thick pipes only on long straight modules, simple rivets; repeatable quiet design. Transparent background outside wall modules. Not a room, no floors. Two related choices for factory floors 4-5.
